page.layout: One column of running text, the full page. No marginal notes, no headings, no running head. Page number at the head. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: non est hoc versari prorsum furfum deor-sum, & corde, ac mente vacuum esse? Debile hoc effugium est: plures habent Synó-dos, ergo iam sunt causa superiores ipsi, & Latini minus habent. Ariani etiam pro una Nicæna Catholicorum viginti, & amplius Synodos Arianas opponent. Esto ergo in meditullio Latinorum una, quæ est contra Photium; quæ erunt utrinque, quibus se ex-tollunt Græci? Prima plane non est, quæ censura Synodali superveniente ab ipsis Græcis extinguitur in hac postrema; cum omnia dicta, factaque contra Photium, & Ignatium, & æque ambo pares, non tantum ipsæ, sed & qui eas recipiunt, condemnen-tur, ut infrà videbimus. Quare condemnata una pro Photio contra Ignatium, & una pro Ignatio contra Photium in hisce tribus Sy-nodis, qua ratione binis Græci se extollant, non dum capio. Narrant Veteres, Margitem Homericum non ultra quinque ad calculos potuisse reducere, οὐ δ᾽ ἓ φασιν ἀπηχώς[?]. At præsens hic calculator, cum in tribus deliret, erit ipso Margite infipientior. Quod luculen-ter docet Juris Græco-Romani Magnates peritis-simi Zonaras, & Balsamon, qui elisa duarum e medio, quam Latini pro Octava generali ample-ctuntur, hanc Primam, & Tertiam Oecumenicas, Primam, & Secundā Constantinopolitanam nun-

page.notes: Faded and stained in places, with no legible marginal notes on this page. The Greek phrase after "reducere," is printed faintly. I read it as οὐ δ᾽ ἓ φασιν ἀπηχώς, but the accents and the word division are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The text runs on across the page with no printed indents, so it is one paragraph continued from the previous page and into the next. Spelling was normalised only for u/v and i/j, as the rules require. The catchword "cu-" was read from the lower right.
